LESSON: HUMAN ORIGIN

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: People, Population and Relationships (28 lessons)
Topic 2.1: Human Origin
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 5

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Human Origin, part of People, Population and Relationships (28 lessons) in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How did human beings come to be?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. sign terms and concepts related to people, population and relationships,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Human Origin in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. explore traditional stories of human origin from African communities,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Human Origin in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Human Origin in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Human Origin in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Human Origin together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: learners develop the skill of listening and observing as they interact with the resource person and

recognise the value of others' ideas as they work in groups to compare the different stories on human origin from their communities and

share in class.

● Learning to learn: learners develop researching skills as they conduct an online or library research and write a collaborative essay on

traditional and religious stories of human origin.

Values:
● Responsibility: learners develop responsibility as they work in groups to compare different stories on human origin.

● Patriotism: learners develop patriotism as they write a collaborative essay on traditional and religious stories of human origin.

● Respect: learners exhibit respect for others as they engage a resource person to discuss the traditional and religious stories on human

origin.

Link to other subjects:

• English: learners relate to writing skills as they write a collaborative essay on traditional and religious stories of human origin.

• Religious Education: learners engage a resource person to discuss the religious stories on human origin.

Suggested Learning Resources:

local and extended environment, photographs, pictures and paintings , internet sources, digital resources, approved textbooks and other

printed resources, artefacts, museum, monuments, cultural and historical sites, newspaper cuttings, libraries, posters, charts,
